question: How many members of the Rajya Sabha can be nominated by the President of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: 100
12
50
9
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 12

Explanation:
According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, the President can nominate 12 members to the Rajya Sabha. These members are people having special knowledge or practical experience in fields like art, literature, science, and social service. The total strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245, of which 233 members represent states and union territories, while 12 are nominated by the President. This provision ensures expertise and diversity in Parliament. Nominated members have the same rights and privileges as elected members, but they can be removed by the President. Their term is also six years, subject to the usual rules of retirement.

☛ What is the term of nominated members? → 6 years
☛ How many members represent states in Rajya Sabha? → 233
☛ From which fields are nominated members chosen? → Art, literature, science, social service
☛ Can nominated members vote in Presidential elections? → Yes

question: When Pitt's India Act was passed? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: 1784
1857
1909
1773
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1784

Explanation:
The Pitt's India Act, also known as the Government of India Act 1784, was passed by the British Parliament. This act aimed to establish control over the political and administrative functions of the East India Company. It created the Board of Control to oversee the company's affairs. The act was introduced to address the shortcomings of the Regulating Act of 1773. Pitt's India Act ended the system of Dual Government in the company and centralized the administration. This act was passed when William Pitt the Younger was the Prime Minister of Britain.

question_hi: पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट कब पारित हुआ? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))

Explanation:
पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट, जिसे भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1784 के नाम से भी जाना जाता है, ब्रिटिश संसद द्वारा पारित किया गया था। इस अधिनियम का उद्देश्य ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के राजनीतिक और प्रशासनिक कार्यों पर नियंत्रण स्थापित करना था। इसके तहत, कंपनी के मामलों की देखरेख के लिए नियंत्रण बोर्ड (Board of Control) बनाया गया। यह अधिनियम 1773 के रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट की कमियों को दूर करने के लिए लाया गया था। पिट्स इंडिया एक्ट ने कंपनी में दोहरी सरकार (Dual Government) की व्यवस्था को समाप्त किया और प्रशासन को अधिक केंद्रीकृत किया। यह अधिनियम तब पारित हुआ जब विलियम पिट द यंगर ब्रिटेन के प्रधानमंत्री थे।

question: The subject related to sports come in which list of the Indian constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: Residual List
Central List
Concurrent list
State List
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State List

Explanation:
In the Indian Constitution, the subject of sports and entertainment comes under the State List. The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List. Subjects like sports, recreation, and education are included in the State List, giving state governments the power to legislate on these matters. This reflects the federal structure where states have autonomy over regional issues. However, national sports bodies and certain major events may also involve central government.

question_hi: खेल से संबंधित विषय भारतीय संविधान की किस सूची में आते हैं? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))

समवर्ती सूची

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में खेल और मनोरंजन से संबंधित विषय राज्य सूची के अंतर्गत आते हैं। राज्य सूची में वे विषय शामिल हैं जिन पर राज्य सरकारें कानून बना सकती हैं। संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची में तीन सूचियाँ हैं - केंद्रीय सूची (संघ सूची), राज्य सूची, और समवर्ती सूची। खेल, मनोरंजन और शिक्षा जैसे विषय राज्य सूची के अंतर्गत आते हैं, जिससे राज्यों को इन क्षेत्रों में नीतियाँ बनाने और नियमन करने का अधिकार है। यह संघीय ढाँचे में राज्यों की स्वायत्तता को दर्शाता है। हालांकि, कुछ खेल संगठन और राष्ट्रीय मामले केंद्र सरकार के अधीन भी आ सकते हैं।

question: Who is the only nominal power in the Government of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: President
Vice President
Prime Minister
Speaker
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
According to the Indian Constitution, the President is the constitutional head of the state, but his powers are nominal. The real executive powers lie with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The President acts according to the constitution and laws, and is bound to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Article 74 states that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. The President has some emergency powers, but under normal circumstances, he is only a symbolic head. Thus, the President is the only nominal power in the Government of India.

☛ Who advises the President? → Council of Ministers
☛ Who is the real executive head of India? → Prime Minister
☛ What powers does the President lack? → Real executive powers
☛ On whose advice must the President act? → Council of Ministers

question: Who is the supreme law officer of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: Law and Justice Minister
Advocate General
Attorney General of India
Chief Justice of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Attorney General of India

Explanation:
The supreme law officer of India is the Attorney General of India. This office is established under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution. The Attorney General is appointed by the President and represents the government in the Supreme Court. To be eligible, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court. The Attorney General can participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but cannot vote. They advise the government on legal matters referred by the President. This position is distinct from the Chief Justice of India, who is the head of the judiciary.

question_hi: भारत का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी कौन है? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))

महाधिवक्ता
भारत के महान्यायवादी
भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के महान्यायवादी

Explanation:
भारत का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी महान्यायवादी (Attorney General of India) होता है। यह पद भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 76 के तहत बनाया गया है। महान्यायवादी की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है और वह सर्वोच्च न्यायालय में सरकार का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। यह पद धारण करने के लिए व्यक्ति को सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का न्यायाधीश नियुक्त होने योग्य होना चाहिए। महान्यायवादी संसद के दोनों सदनों में भाग ले सकता है लेकिन वोट नहीं दे सकता। वह राष्ट्रपति द्वारा पूछे गए कानूनी मामलों पर सरकार को सलाह देता है। यह पद भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश से अलग है, जो न्यायपालिका का प्रमुख है।

question: Which of the following provisions of the Indian Constitution can be amended only by the general majority of the two Houses in the Parliament? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: State Policy Directive Principle
Fundamental Rights
Election of Parliament and State Legislature
Representation of States in Parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Election of Parliament and State Legislature

Explanation:
Article 368 of the Indian Constitution describes the amendment procedure. Provisions that can be amended by a simple majority of both Houses include the Election of Parliament and State Legislature, covered under Articles 327 and 328. Other options: Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Rights require a special majority, while Representation of States in Parliament also requires ratification by states. A simple majority means the majority of members present and voting. This provision is related to the electoral system, which can be changed through a simpler procedure.

☛ Which article outlines the amendment procedure? → Article 368
☛ What majority is required to amend Fundamental Rights? → Special majority
☛ What is required to amend Representation of States in Parliament? → Ratification by states
☛ What does simple majority mean? → Majority of members present and voting
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रावधान को संसद के दोनों सदनों के सामान्य बहुमत से ही संशोधित किया जा सकता है? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options_hi: राज्य नीति-निदेशक सिद्धांत
मौलिक अधिकार

संसद में राज्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संसद और राज्य विधानमंडल का चुनाव

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 368 में संशोधन की प्रक्रिया का वर्णन है। संसद के दोनों सदनों के सामान्य बहुमत से संशोधित किए जाने वाले प्रावधानों में संसद और राज्य विधानमंडल का चुनाव शामिल है। यह अनुच्छेद 327 और 328 के अंतर्गत आता है। अन्य विकल्पों में, राज्य नीति-निदेशक सिद्धांत और मौलिक अधिकार को विशेष बहुमत की आवश्यकता होती है, जबकि संसद में राज्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व को राज्यों के अनुमोदन की भी आवश्यकता है। सामान्य बहुमत का अर्थ है उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों का साधारण बहुमत। यह प्रावधान चुनावी प्रणाली से संबंधित है, जिसे सरल प्रक्रिया से बदला जा सकता है।

question: Which ministry does the care of India's National Archives? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Ministry of Environment
Ministry of Culture
Ministry of Commerce
Finance Mantralaya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ministry of Culture

Explanation:
The National Archives of India is under the care of the Ministry of Culture. It is the premier archival institution of the Government of India, responsible for preserving and managing public records. Established in 1891 as the Imperial Record Department in Kolkata, it was moved to New Delhi after the capital shift in 1911. It operates under the Public Records Act, 1993. Being under the Ministry of Culture, it formulates policies for the preservation of historical documents and government archives. The National Archives houses a vast collection of documents from the Mughal period to modern times, serving as a vital resource for researchers and historians.

☛ Which act governs the National Archives? → Public Records Act, 1993
☛ What is the main function of the National Archives? → Preservation and management of public records
☛ Who is the head of the National Archives? → Director General

question: What is the maximum number of members of the Rajya Sabha? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: 150
380
250
368
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 250

Explanation:
The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. According to Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250 members. Out of these, 238 members represent the states and union territories, while 12 members are nominated by the President. These nominated members are persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as art, literature, science, and social service. Currently, the sanctioned strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245, which includes 233 elected members and 12 nominated members. It is a permanent house, and one-third of its members retire every two years.

☛ How are Rajya Sabha members elected? → Indirect election
☛ Who is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha? → Vice President

question: In Political Science, PIL is the full form of the word- (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Primary Interest Litigation
Public Intermediate Law
Public Interest Litigation
Principal Intermediate Law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public Interest Litigation

Explanation:
PIL stands for Public Interest Litigation, which is a legal mechanism allowing any citizen to file a petition in court on behalf of the public interest. In India, PIL was introduced in the 1980s to provide access to justice for the poor and marginalized. It can be filed under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 226 (High Courts). Through PIL, the judiciary has addressed issues like environment, human rights, and corruption, making it a powerful tool for social change. The concept originated in the USA but gained significant importance in India.

☛ When was PIL introduced in India → 1980s
☛ Under which article can PIL be filed in the Supreme Court → Article 32
☛ Under which article can PIL be filed in High Court → Article 226
☛ Which issues are addressed through PIL → Environment, human rights, corruption
question_hi: राजनीति विज्ञान में PIL शब्द का पूर्ण रूप है- (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options_hi: प्राथमिक हित मुकदमेबाजी
सार्वजनिक मध्यवर्ती कानून

प्रिंसिपल इंटरमीडिएट लॉ
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जनहित याचिका

Explanation:
PIL का पूर्ण रूप Public Interest Litigation (जनहित याचिका) है। यह एक कानूनी तंत्र है जो न्यायालय में जनता के हित में मुकदमा दायर करने की अनुमति देता है। भारत में, PIL की शुरुआत 1980 के दशक में हुई, जिससे गरीब और वंचित वर्गों को न्याय तक पहुंच आसान हुई। यह अनुच्छेद 32 (सर्वोच्च न्यायालय) और अनुच्छेद 226 (उच्च न्यायालय) के तहत लाई जा सकती है। PIL के माध्यम से पर्यावरण, मानवाधिकार और भ्रष्टाचार जैसे मुद्दों पर न्यायालय ने महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय दिए हैं।

question: The characteristics of India's "Rule of Law" (law governance) are taken from which of the following constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Japanese Constitution
Irish Constitution
American Constitution
British Constitution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is British Constitution

Explanation:
The concept of 'Rule of Law' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the British Constitution. This principle establishes that law is supreme and no one is above the law. In India, it was elaborated by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in the Constituent Assembly. British jurist A.V. Dicey divided the Rule of Law into three principles: supremacy of law, equality before the law, and predominance of individual rights. Article 14 of the Indian Constitution provides for equality before the law, which is based on this concept. This feature makes India a democratic republic.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ From which constitution is 'Rule of Law' borrowed? → British Constitution
☛ Who propounded this principle? → A.V. Dicey
☛ Which article of Indian Constitution provides equality before law? → Article 14
☛ Who elaborated it in the Constituent Assembly? → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ What are the three principles of Rule of Law? → Supremacy of law, equality, and individual rights
question_hi: भारत के "कानून के शासन" (कानून शासन) की विशेषताएं निम्नलिखित में से किस संविधान से ली गई हैं? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options_hi: जापानी संविधान
आयरिश संविधान
अमेरिकी संविधान
ब्रिटिश संविधान
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ब्रिटिश संविधान

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में 'कानून का शासन' (Rule of Law) की अवधारणा ब्रिटिश संविधान से ली गई है। यह सिद्धांत बताता है कि कानून सर्वोच्च है और कोई भी व्यक्ति कानून से ऊपर नहीं है। भारत में इसकी व्याख्या डॉ. बी.आर. अम्बेडकर ने संविधान सभा में की थी। ब्रिटिश विधिवेत्ता ए.वी. डाइसी ने 'कानून के शासन' को तीन सिद्धांतों में विभाजित किया: कानून की सर्वोच्चता, कानून के समक्ष समानता, और व्यक्तिगत अधिकारों की प्रधानता। भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 में कानून के समक्ष समानता का प्रावधान है, जो इसी अवधारणा पर आधारित है। यह विशेषता भारत को एक लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य बनाती है।

question: Which of the following article of the Indian Constitution is related to "The subject matter of laws created by Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies"? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Article 243
Article 246
Article 248
Article 241
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 246

Explanation:
Article 246 of the Indian Constitution deals with the subject matter of laws made by Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies. It provides for the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States through the three lists in the Seventh Schedule: the Union List (List I), the State List (List II), and the Concurrent List (List III). Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on subjects in the Union List (100 subjects), state legislatures on subjects in the State List (61 subjects), and both on subjects in the Concurrent List (52 subjects). Article 246 ensures that the legislative authority is clearly demarcated, preventing conflicts. This article is fundamental to India's federal structure and defines the scope of central and state legislation.

☛ Article 250 → Parliament's power to legislate on State List subjects during emergency
☛ Article 252 → Parliament's power to legislate with consent of two or more states
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अनुच्छेद "संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं द्वारा बनाए गए कानूनों की विषय-वस्तु" से संबंधित है? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 243
अनुच्छेद 246
अनुच्छेद 248
अनुच्छेद 241
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 246

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 246 भारतीय संविधान का वह अनुच्छेद है जो संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं द्वारा बनाए गए कानूनों की विषय-वस्तु से संबंधित है। यह संघ और राज्य सूचियों के बीच विधायी शक्तियों का वितरण निर्धारित करता है। संघ सूची (सूची I) में 100 विषय हैं जिन पर केवल संसद कानून बना सकती है, राज्य सूची (सूची II) में 61 विषय हैं जिन पर केवल राज्य विधानसभाएं कानून बना सकती हैं, और समवर्ती सूची (सूची III) में 52 विषय हैं जिन पर दोनों कानून बना सकते हैं। अनुच्छेद 246 के तहत, यदि कोई कानून किसी सूची के विषय से संबंधित है, तो वह उस सूची के अनुसार ही बनाया जाएगा। यह अनुच्छेद संघीय ढांचे का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है और सातवीं अनुसूची से जुड़ा है।

question: Who was the first President of the Union Public Service Commission in India? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Dr. A.R. Kidwai
J.P. Gupta
Sir. Ross Barker
Rajani Razdan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sir. Ross Barker

Explanation:
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) was established on 1 October 1926 under the Government of India Act 1919. Its first Chairman was Sir Ross Barker, who served from 1926 to 1932. The UPSC headquarters is located in New Delhi. Dr. A.R. Kidwai later became Chairman, while J.P. Gupta and Rajani Razdan also served as former Chairmen. UPSC conducts recruitment and examinations for civil services in India. It is an independent constitutional body established under Article 315.

question: In 1938, under whose chair was the National Planning Committee established? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))

question: Who is the first citizen of India from among the following? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))

question: The real Head of the Government of India is (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Prime Minister
Speaker of Lok Sabha
Vice President
President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister

Explanation:
In India's parliamentary system, the President is the constitutional head, while the Prime Minister is the real head of the government. The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers and exercises executive powers. According to Articles 74 and 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Prime Minister advises the President, which is binding on him. The Prime Minister is appointed by the President but leads the majority in the Lok Sabha (elected by the people). This system is based on the British model. The Prime Minister is accountable to Parliament and plays a central role in all policy decisions of the government.

question: Which of the following can make laws for peace, progress and good government of Lakshadweep? (RPF Constable 2018 (19/02/2019))
options: Vice President
Prime Minister
President
Chief Justice of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President

Explanation:
Lakshadweep is a Union Territory of India. Under Article 240 of the Indian Constitution, the President has the power to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of certain Union Territories, including Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu. These regulations can repeal or amend any law made by Parliament in relation to these territories. The President exercises this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers. Thus, the authority to legislate specifically for Lakshadweep rests with the President, not with the Vice President, Prime Minister, or Chief Justice.

question: The five year term of the President is calculated from the (RRB JE CE (29/08/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)

question: How many times has 'Financial Emergency' been declared in India so far?  (RRB JE CE (29/08/2019) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: 4 times
5 times
Never
Once
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Never

Explanation:
Article 360 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India is threatened. To date, India has never declared a Financial Emergency. In contrast, a National Emergency (Article 352) has been imposed three times: in 1962, 1971, and 1975. A State Emergency (President's Rule) under Article 356 has been invoked many times. The provisions of a Financial Emergency include central control over financial matters of states. This fact is important for competitive exams as it highlights a unique aspect of Indian federalism where the provision exists but has never been used.
